headline: Build for the web.
Think with AI.
hero.description: A focused 3-month engineering bootcamp in Janakpur. Learn React, Django and practical AI integration—then ship work you can show.
hero.imageAlt: Janakpur Tech Bootcamp students learning together

advantages.text: No disconnected modules. Every week builds directly on the one before it.

items.title: One instructor. One clear path.
items.text: Move from frontend to backend to AI without changing teaching styles or juggling parallel tracks.

items.title: AI that works inside real apps.
items.text: Connect Gemini and OpenAI APIs to useful products—not isolated demos or prompt-only exercises.

items.title: Backend without the setup drama.
items.text: Use Django ORM and SQLite so your attention stays on data models, APIs and product logic.

items.title: A portfolio that is live.
items.text: Ship 10+ GitHub projects and finish with a deployed full-stack capstone ready for Demo Day.

journey.text: Bootcamps built capability. Hackathons tested it. Each milestone moved Janakpur’s technology community forward in a different way.

items.title: The first full-stack cohort
items.story: We opened our first focused learning room around React, Django and the habits of practical software development.
items.result: Students moved beyond college theory and began building, versioning and presenting working web applications.

items.title: Janakpur builds under pressure
items.story: The city’s first community hackathon brought teams together to move from problem statements to working prototypes.
items.result: Local builders could collaborate, make technical decisions quickly and present their ideas to a judging panel.

items.title: A deeper move into data and AI
items.story: The second cohort expanded the program into Python, machine learning and intelligent systems through project-led sessions.
items.result: Learners gained a practical path into AI by working with datasets, models and real application ideas—not theory alone.

items.title: The community returned to ship again
items.story: A second rapid-build sprint gave new teams the same intense cycle of ideation, coding, feedback and final demos.
items.result: The first event was not a one-off. Janakpur now had a repeatable stage for teamwork, competition and youth innovation.

items.title: A regional conversation about AI
items.story: We brought speakers, students and technology enthusiasts into one room for ideas, questions and community connection.
items.result: The community gained direct access to industry perspectives and a larger vision for technology leadership in Madhesh.

items.title: Full-stack engineering meets AI
items.story: The new program joins modern frontend, dependable backend architecture and practical AI APIs in one sequential path.
items.result: Ten-plus GitHub projects and a deployed full-stack AI capstone built for a live portfolio and Demo Day.

curriculum.text: A professionally structured pathway from modern frontend development to backend engineering, applied AI and production delivery.

faq.text: Quick answers about eligibility, learning, projects and the application process.

items.question: Who can apply?
items.answer: Students with basic programming knowledge in C, C++ or Java and a foundation in HTML and CSS can apply.

items.question: Do I need to know Python or React?
items.answer: No. Both are taught during the program. Basic programming logic is enough to get started.

items.question: How are students selected?
items.answer: Admission includes a short, friendly screening interview covering your fundamentals, motivation and availability.

items.question: What will I learn?
items.answer: You will learn modern frontend development, Python and Django APIs, full-stack integration, applied AI and cloud deployment.

items.question: Is the bootcamp practical?
items.answer: Yes. Classes combine concept instruction, live coding and guided hands-on practice, with regular project work.

items.question: What will I build?
items.answer: You will create portfolio projects and finish with a deployed, AI-enabled full-stack capstone product.

items.question: Do I need my own laptop?
items.answer: Yes. A working laptop is required, with 8GB RAM recommended for a smooth development experience.

items.question: How is the schedule managed?
items.answer: The calendar includes organized teaching, practice, review and project sessions. Any schedule changes will be shared in advance.

items.question: How do I register?
items.answer: Select Register Now, complete the application form and wait for the screening details.

finalCta.text: Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. Start with a short registration, then meet us for a friendly screening conversation.
